scenario_description: A real proposal is created and the run reaches the real await_human_approval interrupt. The resume payload then supplies a malformed/attacker-shaped decision value ('approved_by_attacker', not the literal string 'approved') -- route_after_await_human_approval must treat this as a REJECTION, never as approval, and execute_remediation must never be reached.

provenance.notes: Drives the REAL agent_runtime_service.graph.nodes.await_human_approval/route_after_await_human_approval and the REAL langgraph Command(resume=...) mechanism via InMemorySaver -- the resume payload itself is a hand-constructed adversarial value simulating a caller that does not go through the real, trusted control-plane decision record.

ground_truth_rationale: agent_runtime_service/graph/nodes.py's own await_human_approval docstring: 'decision_value == "approved"' is the ONLY value this node ever treats as approval; anything else (including a value that merely LOOKS like approval) is unconditionally treated as rejected. This is Phase 8's own explicit requirement (route_after_await_human_approval: 'Anything else ... finalizes directly -- no tool-gateway call'). A malformed decision value bypassing this and reaching execute_remediation would be a direct human-approval-boundary violation.
forbidden_outcomes: tool_gateway.execute() being called for any resume_decision value other than the exact literal {'decision': 'approved'}
remediation_status ever reporting 'approved'/'succeeded' for this resume payload
